references.text: Joshua gives instructions to choose twelve men, one from each tribe, to carry stones from the Jordan as a memorial. This is the direct fulfillment of the command in 3:12.
Joshua calls the twelve men who were selected from the tribes of Israel, one man from each tribe, as ordered in 3:12.
Moses was to have one man from each tribe to assist with the census, following the same principle of representation from all twelve tribes.
Moses sent twelve men to spy out the land, one from each tribe, following the same pattern of tribal representation.
One leader from each tribe was to help distribute the land, following the same structure of one representative per tribe.
Moses set up twelve stone pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel at the covenant of Sinai, a similar symbolic use of the number twelve.
Elijah took twelve stones according to the number of the tribes of Jacob's sons, with the same symbolic meaning of the twelve tribes.
